entry.label: Structural coupling
entry.description: Repeated system-environment interaction can shape the structures through which further interaction occurs. The FEM project uses this idea to identify consequential enterprise-environment relationships; that application is narrower than the biological concept.
entry.canonical_definition: Repeated interactions through which systems and their environments shape the structures governing later interactions. In Maturana's biological account, these structural changes conserve the system's defining organisation.

profile.title: Structural coupling
profile.summary: Maturana distinguishes a perturbation that triggers change from an instruction that specifies it: the current structure determines the response. Fractal Enterprise Model practice uses structural coupling to examine consequential enterprise–environment relationships; that application requires its own account of the participating systems and interactions.
profile.canonical_definition: Repeated interactions through which systems and their environments shape the structures governing later interactions. In Maturana's biological account, these structural changes conserve the system's defining organisation.
profile.why_it_matters: A repeated message can meet a changing recipient. Communication problems may involve the history of the relationship as well as the message.
practice_connections: Trace how repeated interactions alter the parties' capacity to respond; treat this as an interpretive question, not a biological diagnosis.
common_misreadings: An external message determines the recipient's response.
open_checks: Evidence is needed for any proposed organisational application.
profile.editorial_note: Primary passages checked for this bounded research pass. Exposition and editorial comparisons remain distinct; named editorial acceptance is not implied by publication.
